core_summary: Electric circuits require a continuous closed path for current to flow from a source of electrical energy (cell/battery) through conductors to electrical devices (bulbs, LEDs). An electric cell has a positive (+ cap) and negative (- disc) terminal. Connecting cells positive-to-negative in series creates a battery. Circuit diagrams use universally standardized symbols. Incandescent bulbs rely on a glowing heated filament, while Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs) emit light efficiently when current flows in one specific direction (longer lead = positive, shorter lead = negative).
key_concepts: To construct a simple functional switch using safety pins and drawing pins.

key_terms.definition: Conventional current flows from the positive (+) terminal of the power source to the negative (-) terminal.
A semiconductor light source that permits electric current flow in only one forward direction.

key_takeaways: Electric current is not consumed; electrical energy is converted into thermal and radiant light energy while charge continues flowing back to the negative terminal.
An LED is a polar semiconductor light source. Lead identification: Longer lead = Positive (+) Anode; Shorter lead = Negative (-) Cathode. Forward-Bias...
